observations: Photo 0 shows a DSLR with a Nikon logo on the top and a large lens mount; the body has a visible model marking area that appears to read D610.
Photo 1 shows the same Nikon DSLR from a similar angle; Nikon branding is clear.
Photo 2 shows the top/rear controls and a rear LCD; the camera body is clearly Nikon, and the top dial area is visible.

claims.claim: Used Nikon D610 in good condition.
claims.evidence: Photos show a Nikon DSLR body, but condition (sensor, shutter count, autofocus, buttons, LCD health) is not testable from these images.

claims.claim: May show sign of cosmetic wears.
claims.evidence: Cosmetic wear is not clearly assessable (no close-ups of scratches/dents; lighting glare).
No accessories are shown in the provided photos; the text is truncated and cannot be verified remotely.
Photos show Nikon branding on the camera top (photo 0 and photo 1), not Canon.

risks.risk: Brand/model mismatch risk: seller text says Canon, but photos show Nikon D610. This can mean wrong item, swapped listing, or confusion about what’s being sold.
risks.proof: Ask for a photo of the camera with the seller’s handwritten note showing the exact model (Nikon D610) and the listing date, plus a close-up of the model text on the body.
risks.if_unproven: Price as Nikon D610 body only (worst case for missing accessories), and treat any Canon claim as unreliable.

risks.risk: Accessory completeness risk (battery/charger/other items not shown).
risks.proof: Request a single photo laid out: battery, charger, cables, strap, and any included items, all together and clearly labeled.
risks.if_unproven: Price as body only (no guaranteed battery/charger).

risks.risk: Functional risk (shutter count, autofocus, metering, buttons, LCD, and sensor condition not testable from photos).
risks.proof: Request a short video showing: power on, menu navigation, autofocus on a moving subject, and a sample photo at a normal setting (plus a close-up of the LCD showing no dead pixels).
risks.if_unproven: Price as not fully proven/assume typical used wear and possible faults; do not price at “good working” premium.

risks.risk: Cosmetic damage risk (scratches/dents around mount, grips, and top dials not shown in close-up).
risks.proof: Request close-up photos of: lens mount area, top dials, grip edges, and any visible scuffs with flash.
risks.if_unproven: Price at the lower end of the comparable range.

proof_requests: Confirm the exact item: send a close-up photo of the model marking (D610) and a photo of the full camera with a handwritten note matching the listing.
Show all included accessories in one laid-out photo (battery, charger, cables/strap, and anything else).
Provide a short test video: power on + menu + autofocus on a moving object + take one sample photo.
Send close-ups of lens mount, top dials, and grip edges (with flash) to assess cosmetic damage.
response.reason: The photos clearly show a Nikon D610, but the seller’s text says Canon and the accessories/working condition are not verifiable from the images. Without proof of the exact package and functionality, a confident price pick isn’t safe.
